core.title: Declare a device-width viewport in every full HTML document
core.given: Any full HTML document in scope: a static markup page, a presentation layout that renders the full document, or a template that builds one (the artifact kinds the profile lists as markup kinds)
core.when: the document exists in the repository (new or existing)
core.then: The document declares `<meta name="viewport">` whose content sets `width=device-width`.
prefer: Declare `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` in each full document and keep zoom available.
During GREEN: add or correct the single viewport declaration in the document/layout that serves the current behavior.
During GREEN: reuse the existing shared layout when one owns the document head.
avoid: Blocking zoom (MUST NOT): `user-scalable=no` or a `maximum-scale` below 2.
unless: Fragments that are not full documents (no root `<html>` element) are out of scope.
core.why: Without a device-width viewport a phone renders a zoomed-out desktop layout, whatever the CSS says. Blocking zoom fails users who need to enlarge text, also an accessibility failure.
evidence: The current browser-rendered acceptance test passes.
The full document declares device width (`width=device-width`) in its viewport meta and permits zoom.
verification: Scope: every artifact of the profile's markup kinds that holds, renders or builds a full document; files without the root `<html>` element are fragments and are skipped. All in-scope documents are checked, not only changed ones.
Never scan vendored and generated trees; the exact trees this check never scans are owned by the realization's validator (checker-owned scope), not by the profile's stack-wide exclusion list.
Fail when the viewport meta is absent, or its content lacks `width=device-width`, or it contains `user-scalable=no` or a `maximum-scale` value below 2. Each condition alone is a finding.

fires: An existing markup file containing the root `<html>` element has no viewport meta.
A presentation layout rendering the full document declares a viewport whose content lacks `width=device-width` (zoom otherwise allowed).
A template building a full document sets `user-scalable=no` or a `maximum-scale` below 2.
A presentation layout renders the full document with other meta tags but no viewport meta.
doesNotFire: A markup fragment or partial template with no root `<html>` element.
Files under the vendored or generated trees the check never scans.

profileRequirements.meaning: The artifact kinds that can hold, render or build a full HTML document and are therefore candidates for this rule; the core's given, activation fact and verifier scope are instantiated from them.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `.html`/`.htm` files; `.tsx`/`.jsx` layouts that render `<html>`; `.ts`/`.js` templates that build a full document

bunOnly.text: Viewport `content` given as a JSX expression (`content={VIEWPORT}`): the meta must be present; its value is not judged.
bunOnly.reason: Bun grants this exemption solely to JSX attribute expressions; generalizing it to any statically unreadable value would also exempt dynamic content in non-JSX templates that Bun still judges, weakening the check. The exception's exact scope is therefore realization-owned and not asserted by the neutral core.

bunOnly.text: If `content` is a JSX expression (`content={...}`), it cannot be read statically: require presence of the meta only, do not judge the value.
bunOnly.reason: Same JSX-only exemption in its verifier form; the core carries no general statically-unreadable-value exception, so this instruction and its exact JSX scope stay with the Bun realization.

neutralityNotes: The regulated artifact is the HTML viewport meta element and its content directives (`width=device-width`, `user-scalable`, `maximum-scale`); these are web-platform standards shared by every realization of this rule, so they remain in the core. Stack-specific and kept in bunOnly: the file kinds/suffixes that hold, render or build a document (profile: idiom.markup_kinds); this validator's exact never-scanned trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`), which are checker-owned scope and deliberately NOT presented as the stack-wide roots.excluded union (the core only keeps the deference in verification); the JSX-expression exemption for viewport `content`, which Bun grants solely to JSX attribute expressions — generalizing it to any statically unreadable value would let non-JSX templates escape the device-width and zoom checks, so the exception is realization-owned and the core asserts none; and the detector/validator/finding ids. Per the Bun sidecar's declared split, `then` carries only the device-width obligation while the zoom prohibition stays coder-facing as avoid[1] (MUST NOT); the proposed companion convention remains a realization-side split suggestion and is not asserted by the neutral core. Severity 3 and the strict disposition are carried in core verification, not in the profile.
